svg.text: Randomized Algorithms — Las Vegas & Monte Carlo
Las Vegas vs Monte Carlo
• Las Vegas: always correct, expected runtime varies
→ Randomized QuickSort: O(n log n) expected, O(n²) worst
→ Randomized QuickSelect: O(n) expected
• Monte Carlo: fixed runtime, correct with high probability
→ Miller-Rabin primality test: O(k log²n) with error prob 4⁻ᵏ
→ Bloom filter membership: no false negatives, bounded false +
→ Karger's min-cut: O(V²) per trial, run O(V² log V) times
Randomized QuickSort & QuickSelect
• QuickSort: pick pivot uniformly at random from subarray
→ Each element is pivot O(log n) times in expectation
→ E[comparisons] = 2n ln n ≈ 1.39 n log₂ n
→ Adversarial inputs impossible: random pivot defeats sorted input
• QuickSelect: find kth smallest — only recurse into one partition
→ E[comparisons] = O(n) — T(n) = T(n/2) + O(n) on average
→ Worst case O(n²) but probability exponentially small
Hashing & Probabilistic Techniques
• Universal hashing: family H where Pr[h(x)=h(y)] ≤ 1/m for x≠y
→ Expected O(1) ops per hash table operation
• 2-universal: Pr[h(x)=h(y)] ≤ 1/m — sufficient for chaining
• Reservoir sampling: sample k items from stream of unknown size n
→ each item i: keep with prob k/i, replace random kept item
• Treap: BST with random priorities → expected O(log n) height
• Skip list: each node promoted with prob p → O(log n) expected
• Rabin-Karp: rolling hash for O(n+m) expected string matching
• Randomized MST (Karger-Klein-Tarjan): O(E) expected
Analysis Techniques & Applications
• Linearity of expectation: E[X+Y] = E[X]+E[Y] always
→ QuickSort analysis: E[comparisons] = Σᵢ<ⱼ Pr[i compared to j]
• Markov inequality: Pr[X ≥ t] ≤ E[X]/t (one-sided bound)
• Chernoff bound: tail bound for sum of independent RVs
→ Pr[X ≥ (1+δ)μ] ≤ e^(-δ²μ/3) for δ ≤ 1
• Load balancing: n balls into n bins → max load O(log n/log log n)
• Power of two choices: max load O(log log n) — used in NGINX
• Applications: distributed systems, crypto, approx algorithms
Las Vegas: always correct
Monte Carlo: correct w.h.p.
QuickSort: E[O(n log n)]
QuickSelect: E[O(n)]
Power of 2 choices: O(log log n) load
